name: FastAPI routers, dependencies, lifespan, OpenAPI
short_definition: FastAPI is the default Python ASGI web framework for engineer services: Starlette-based routing, Pydantic v2 request/response validation, dependency injection via Depends/Annotated, lifespan context for resource lifecycle, and automatic OpenAPI. As of 2026-07-13 PyPI latest is 0.139.0. Use for Python HTTP APIs, SSE/LLM token streams, and BFF-adjacent services — not as a Next.js replacement for UI.
scope_in: App factory, APIRouter modular layout, include_router
Depends / Annotated dependency patterns (auth, DB session, settings)
lifespan async context manager for pools, models, clients
Request validation, status codes, exception handlers
BackgroundTasks (short only) vs real job queues
Integration with uvicorn/granian as ASGI servers
scope_out: Next.js Server Actions / Route Handlers (TS BFF path)
Serving HTML SPAs as primary product shell

defaults.layout: src/<pkg>/main.py app factory; routers/ by domain; deps.py for Annotated deps; lifespan for resources
defaults.di: Annotated[T, Depends(...)] aliases (e.g. CurrentUser) — not raw Depends in every signature
defaults.lifecycle: lifespan= asynccontextmanager only; @app.on_event startup/shutdown is deprecated
defaults.openapi: response_model on mutating and public GETs; tags + prefix per router; disable docs in prod if threat model requires
defaults.async: async def for I/O handlers; def only for pure CPU-light sync; never block event loop
defaults.server: uvicorn for local; production per py-asgi-servers

use_when: Python service needs HTTP JSON API, OpenAPI, or SSE
Shared validation + schema for external clients
Team already on async SQLAlchemy / httpx stack
do_not_use_when: Ultra-low-latency / high-throughput binary protocols → consider Rust/Axum
Simple Supabase-only CRUD from browser with RLS — may not need Python service
Sync Django monolith already shipping — don't rewrite for fashion

alternatives.starlette: Bare ASGI if you need less magic
alternatives.litestar: If msgspec-first and DI style preferred

do: Use lifespan for DB pools, httpx.AsyncClient, Redis, ML model load
APIRouter(prefix=..., tags=..., dependencies=[...]) for cross-cutting router auth
Central AppError → exception handler; never leak stack traces in prod
Health routes outside heavy auth middleware when probes need them
dont: Don't put business logic in path operation functions — keep handlers thin
Don't create global engines/clients at import time without test escape hatches
Don't use BackgroundTasks for multi-minute or must-not-lose work
Don't return ORM objects directly without schema

code_skeleton:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated, AsyncIterator

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class ItemCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)

class ItemOut(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str

class AppState:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.ready = False

state = AppState()

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    # startup: pools, clients, warm caches
    state.ready = True
    yield
    # shutdown: close pools/clients
    state.ready = False

PROD = False  # from settings
app = FastAPI(title="service", lifespan=lifespan, docs_url=None if PROD else "/docs")

async def get_current_user() -> str:
    # replace with real JWT/session dependency
    return "user_123"

CurrentUser = Annotated[str, Depends(get_current_user)]

router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1/items", tags=["items"])

@router.post("", response_model=ItemOut, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def create_item(body: ItemCreate, user: CurrentUser) -> ItemOut:
    if not state.ready:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="not ready")
    return ItemOut(id="itm_1", name=body.name)

@app.get("/healthz")
async def healthz() -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"status": "ok" if state.ready else "starting"}

app.include_router(router)
failure_modes: Import-time side effects load DB/ML even in unit tests → slow/flaky CI
Sync ORM or time.sleep in async route → event loop stall
Missing lifespan teardown → connection leaks under reload/k8s churn
Depends yield not closed on exceptions → pool exhaustion
OpenAPI models out of sync with actual responses (response_model=None everywhere)
CORS misconfig blocks browser BFF or over-opens credentials
Exception handlers return internal details in production
anti_patterns: Monolithic main.py with 50 routes and no routers
on_event startup + lifespan mixed (docs: lifespan disables events)
Global mutable singletons without lifespan ownership
HTTPException for domain control flow deep in services
Agent scaffolding Flask/Django REST for greenfield async services
Notebooks exported as FastAPI apps without structure

deprecation_watch: Pydantic v1 BaseSettings / .dict() / .parse_obj — v2 model_dump / model_validate
Flask + marshmallow greenfield for new async APIs
apiapp = FastAPI() per module without include_router discipline
ts_boundary: Next.js remains UI + cookie SSR auth shell. Call Python FastAPI for AI, heavy compute, long SSE, or shared multi-client OpenAPI. Generate TS clients from OpenAPI (openapi-typescript / orval) rather than hand-written fetch types. Do not duplicate business rules in both Server Actions and FastAPI without a single source of truth.
rust_boundary: Prefer Axum when p99/cpu cost justifies (see rust.md). Keep FastAPI for iteration speed on AI glue and CRUD-ish services. Same OpenAPI-ish contract discipline at the edge; don't rewrite working FastAPI without measured need.
supabase_boundary: Prefer direct Postgres (async SQLAlchemy/asyncpg) from FastAPI for service-role server paths; use supabase-py only when matching client SDK features. Never expose service role to browser. RLS still applies for user-scoped data; service bypass must be explicit and audited.
boundary_contracts: OpenAPI 3 as contract artifact in CI
Shared error JSON shape {error, code, request_id}
Auth: Bearer JWT or mTLS service-to-service; align claims with Supabase JWT if used
Migrations owned by Alembic or Supabase — one writer

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: HTTP JSON/SSE API in product backend
decision_matrix_row.python: FastAPI default for AI services, workers' control plane, OpenAPI APIs
decision_matrix_row.ts: Next Server Actions / Route Handlers for same-app BFF mutations

threats: AuthZ gaps if Depends only on some routes
SSRF via user-supplied URLs in server-side fetch
OpenAPI docs exposing internal models in production
mitigations: Pydantic models with explicit fields; forbid extras where appropriate
Router-level dependencies for auth on protected prefixes
Allowlist outbound URLs; timeouts on httpx
docs_url/redoc_url/openapi_url None in prod or protect with network policy

must_not_generate: Bare global database connections without lifecycle
sync blocking I/O in async routes
Flask scaffolds for new Python services

tests_required: OpenAPI schema smoke (path exists, security schemes if any)

negative: BackgroundTasks used for payments/emails without queue
response_model omitted on all POST handlers

skill_module_bullets: Default Python HTTP framework: FastAPI 0.139.x + Pydantic v2 as_of 2026-07-13
lifespan only for startup/shutdown; on_event is deprecated
Routers + Annotated Depends; thin handlers; domain pure
OpenAPI is the TS contract; generate clients, don't invent parallel types
BackgroundTasks ≠ job queue; escalate to arq/Taskiq/Temporal for durability
Health endpoints + exception handlers without internal leak
